text:
sec-oncall: Security advisory P1: possible exposure of our code-signing private key used for internal package signing. Detected by CI verify job failing signature checks after an automated mirror pull. Immediate org action required.
sec-oncall: Impact: any packages signed with the key since 2026-03-24 00:00 UTC should be considered suspect; installs should be paused until verification.
ci-bot: automated alert: package-sign-verify job failed: signature mismatch for package redwood-cli v1.13.0 pulled from mirror pypi-mirror-1 at 2026-03-25T09:37Z.
pkg-admin: ack. Which key fingerprint are we talking about?
sig-ops: fingerprint: 3A:7D:4B:9C:AA:11:55:EE:22:77:88:66:CC:01:99:00. Key alias: redwood-code-sign-2025.
alice: running immediate verify across all signed packages since 2026-03-24: `sigctl verify --since 2026-03-24 --key-alias redwood-code-sign-2025 | tee /tmp/sig-verify.out`
bob: I'm disabling auto-publish pipelines that use the signing step and enabling manual gating. Patch incoming to infra/publishers to require approval.
sec-oncall: Required actions for package owners: 1) Stop installs of affected packages (block in internal index). 2) Re-run signature verification for your package builds. 3) If mismatch, quarantine artifact and revoke trust in the signing key. 4) Rotate signing key if compromise confirmed.
sig-ops: cross-checking HSM logs now for key export events. HSM audit: no export op recorded in the last 90 days, but there are two unexpected HSM admin logins on 2026-03-24 23:55 UTC from IP 203.0.113.45. Investigating.
ci-bot: note: mirror re-hydration job pulled signed artifacts from vendor mirror at 2026-03-25T09:30Z. Source mirrors: mirror-a, mirror-b.
pkg-admin: quarantined redwood-cli v1.13.0 and flagged index entry as untrusted. Will notify integrators to pin to v1.12.4.
legal: please preserve all logs and prepare for potential disclosure communication if we confirm key compromise.
alice: running `cosign verify-blob` and `sigctl verify` across wheels and tarballs. Posting results in 15m.
bob: rotating signing key plan: generate new key in HSM with `hsmctl generate --alias redwood-code-sign-2026`, update signing workflows to use new alias, and publish new public cert to keyring. ETA ~1h if HSM rotation allowed.
sig-ops: hold on rotation until we validate whether the private key actually left the HSM. Rotation is fine, but we need forensic evidence first.
eng-manager: exec ask: prepare a short one-paragraph summary for CTO once we have containment status.
devrel: drafting user guidance: "If you communicate with customers, advise to pin to last known-good versions and avoid auto-updates until verification completes."
ci-bot: automated job results: verify sweep found 5 packages with signature mismatches out of 213 checked (list: redwood-cli@1.13.0, redwood-sdk-py@0.9.1, redwood-utils@2.2.0rc1, redwood-agent@0.4.0).
sig-ops: HSM vendor contacted for urgent support; escalated P1 ticket with vendor.
alice: found that the mismatched artifacts differ by a single added file `suspicious.sh` in tarballs. Capturing samples and uploading to secure evidence bucket.
bob: temporarily publishing a revocation entry in our keyring and setting index policy to reject packages signed with redwood-code-sign-2025 until cleared.
legal: if we need to notify customers, coordinate timing: we must confirm scope first.
sec-oncall: containment summary: auto-publishes paused, affected artifacts quarantined, HSM logs under forensics, publishing plumbing set to manual, signing key rotation plan drafted. Next update in 30m. If you see additional mismatches, add to this thread and ping @sig-ops. :lock:
